text:
Maya: Heads up — saw tenant-A's traffic suddenly land on the generic backup model after the circuit-breaker kicked. Header override `x-tenant-route` didn't seem to be honored when CB fired. Repro steps below.

Liam: ugh, that sounds bad. do you have the raw request/headers and the route config?

Maya: yeah quick paste:
```
POST /v1/chat
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
x-tenant-route: tenant-a
Content-Type: application/json
{ "model": "gptx-4-std", "input": "..." }
```
Route config (simplified):
```yaml
- matcher: path_prefix:/v1/chat
  priority: 100
  tenant_header: x-tenant-route
  fallback_chain: [gptx-4-small, gptx-3-std, passthru]
```
When the CB tripped we ended up in `passthru` (generic fallback) even though tenant-a has a pinned backup `gptx-4-small`.

Pranav: Hmm. I think this is the old ordering bug — header overrides were applied after we evaluate CB eligibility. If CB evaluation rewrites route to a degraded lane early, header-based routing gets skipped.

Irene: Noted. That would explain why only tenant-scoped backups are bypassed on surge. Does CB have visibility into header-derived lanes?

Pranav: Not right now. CB only looks at route_id + global capacity tag. It doesn't introspect tenant_header before deciding to short-circuit.

Maya: Repro showed: with low capacity, first request triggered CB, CB returned `ROUTE_DEGRADED` and the runtime forwarded to the global degraded lane. No attempt to match tenant-specific fallbacks.

Liam: Two options: 1) change evaluation order so header-derived matcher runs before CB check, or 2) extend CB to consider `tenant_header` and prefer tenant backups. Both have tradeoffs.

Irene: Order change is simpler but riskier — CB exists to short-circuit expensive matching during big bursts. Running full matcher could add latency at the very moment we want cheap checks.

Pranav: Agreed. Maybe a hybrid: fast-path CB that checks a small set of attributes including `tenant_header` (cheap hash lookup). If a tenant has a pinned backup, prefer that; otherwise fallback to the current global degrade.

Maya: That sounds reasonable. For immediate mitigation we could add an explicit `cb_exceptions: [tenant_header]` flag on the route so tenant-aware backups bypass the very-first CB. Short-term config change.

Liam: Can we add a quick config toggle and ship as a canary to a subset of routes? We'll need telemetry to verify.

Irene: We'll need metrics: `route.resolve.overrides` (count when header override applied), `cb.evaluated.shortcircuit` with tags for `tenant` and `route_id`, and `fallback.path` to see which fallback was chosen.

Pranav: I'll throw together a patch:
```diff
+ // in cb_evaluator: check tenant header hash against pinned-backups map
+ if (tenant_header && pinned_backups.contains(tenant_header)) {
+   choose(pinned_backups[tenant_header]);
+   return CB_HANDLED;
+ }
```
We'll keep the existing fast-path intact and only add the O(1) hash lookup.

Maya: ack. also add an info-level log when tenant-specific backup selected so we can correlate with request IDs for debugging.

Liam: Once Pranav has a branch, let's canary to 10% of requests for routes with `cb_exceptions: tenant_header`. Postgres of rollout: 30m ramp, check `latency.p50`, `cost.per_token`, and the new `fallback.path` distribution.

sre-bot: incident-alert — CB surge detected on cluster-gamma at 2026-03-04T15:12:44Z (auto-throttled).

Pranav: branch up in ~30m. I'll include unit tests for header present/absent and an integration test simulating burst.

Irene: Also update Console UX: in Rollouts we should show `cb_exceptions` in the config diff and surface the `fallback.path` histogram on the route page so customers can see if tenant backups are being used.

Maya: thanks — makes sense. for now i'll flip the config on tenant-A's route to enable `cb_exceptions` and monitor. Will report back in ~45m. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deploy started for pr/4923 -> canary (10%)

Liam: thx team. let's reconvene after the canary window and decide if we promote the change or iterate. :thumbsup:
